solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Reportedly detects change in Washington? (5)

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to sense something is to detect it; say that word aloud and respell it

annotation.surface: A news item about someone in Washington noticing that something has shifted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like a verb or an event; the question mark flags it as loose coins, and in Washington the small coins are cents.
annotation.definitionFit: Change here is loose coins, and the American small coin is the hundredth of a dollar; the question mark marks the regional twist.

entries.clue: Oomph in something like rented carriage (9)

indicators.note: 'in' places BRIO within CA, before LET is added

blocks.note: a let flat is a rented one

annotation.surface: Someone finds a bit of zest in what sounds like a hired coach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Something like rented carriage' reads as one phrase hinting at a cab; in fact 'something like' is CA (circa) and only 'carriage' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain naming of a type: a light two-wheeled, one-horse vehicle, the ancestor of the convertible car that borrowed its name.

entries.clue: Linked group crossed lines in New England? (5)

indicators.note: 'in' sets the crossed lines inside the letters for New England

blocks.note: New England is the north-east of the United States: NE + US
an X is two crossed lines

annotation.surface: A network of people with tangled phone lines somewhere in New England.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that NE US is a description of New England rather than an abbreviation for it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the Latin word for a binding together, used for any connected series or cluster.

entries.clue: Sentimental weakness seconds frequently notice (4,4)

annotation.surface: Someone keeps catching sight of a fondness they can't shake.
annotation.walkthrough: Three short pieces in clue order; the only trick is taking 'seconds' as the single letter S.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: having one for someone means an affectionate partiality you can't help, which is exactly a sentimental weakness.

entries.clue: Awful writing perhaps in Old English message (9)

indicators.note: 'in' puts the writing letter within the message word

blocks.note: writing is one of the three Rs

annotation.surface: A critic dismisses some badly written note in Old English.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old English' pretends to be one thing (OE); it splits into EX and E. The three Rs are reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic, so writing is an R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from Latin for 'accursed', it now means extremely bad, as in a dreadful performance.

entries.clue: Osprey finally leaving nest for lake (4)

indicators.note: 'finally' picks the letter at the very end of osprey
'leaving' means going out of, so that letter departs the nest

blocks.note: an eyrie is a bird of prey's nest

annotation.surface: A young osprey at last flies the nest and heads for the lake.
annotation.walkthrough: The osprey fits the eyrie perfectly, which hides that only its last letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the five Great Lakes, on the US–Canada border.

entries.clue: American after team place for test (6-4)

indicators.note: 'after' places American behind the team and place letters

blocks.note: a football or cricket team is an eleven

annotation.surface: An American secures a spot on a squad for a trial match.
annotation.walkthrough: The eleven-plus is an exam British children once sat at 11 to decide on grammar school entry.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, British: the selection exam sat at the end of primary school.

entries.clue: Slow down on time machine saving lives (6)

indicators.note: 'saving' in its old sense of 'except', so the lives letters are left out

blocks.note: the TARDIS is the time machine in Doctor Who

annotation.surface: A plea to ease off a time machine that is busy rescuing people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saving lives' reads as rescue; 'saving' means except, and 'lives' is IS. The TARDIS is the police-box time machine of the British TV series Doctor Who.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a verb: to delay or hold back progress, from Latin tardus, slow.

entries.clue: Puzzle book retired mum left, consumed by drink (9)

indicators.note: a retired thing withdraws, goes back, so MA turns round
what is consumed is swallowed, so L sits inside BOOZE

annotation.surface: A retired mother leaves a book behind after one drink too many.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'retired mum' with drink as if she were a pensioner; 'retired' just reverses MA.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a verb: to baffle or trick someone.

entries.clue: Grind down before accepting arrangement with bank (5)

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the 'before' word takes the bank letters inside it

blocks.note: OD = overdraft, an arrangement agreed with a bank

annotation.surface: Someone worn down before a bank agrees to lend.
annotation.walkthrough: An agreed overdraft is often called an 'arranged overdraft', which is why OD fits 'arrangement with bank'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to wear away gradually, as water does rock.

entries.clue: Fight cancelled in US — kill ticket seller (3,6)

blocks.note: a match that is off is cancelled
to ice is American slang for to kill

annotation.surface: A called-off bout in America leaves someone ready to murder whoever sold the tickets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In US' attaches to 'kill', not to the fight: ICE is American gangster slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the counter at a theatre or cinema whose job is selling admission.

entries.clue: Revolutionary work gathered speed (5)

indicators.note: a revolution is a turning round, so the letters are turned back to front

annotation.surface: A radical piece of work gains momentum.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary work' looks like a manifesto; the adjective just turns OPMET around.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, chiefly musical: the rate at which a piece is played, and loosely any pace.

entries.clue: Stress at home — little sibling tense (6)

blocks.note: to be in = to be at home
sis is short for sister, a 'little' word for a sibling

annotation.surface: Stress in the house, with a nervous younger sister.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Little sibling' is a short form of the word, not a younger child; and 'Stress' is the verb, as in 'stress a point'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a verb: to lay emphasis on a point, to demand firmly.

entries.clue: Loud organ: two notes terrifying (8)

blocks.note: so and me, notes of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A church organ blasting two notes at frightening volume.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical setting makes 'organ' an instrument; it is the body part. SO and ME are sol-fa spellings of sol and mi.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: inspiring dread, as a formidable opponent does.

entries.clue: Image associated with skull vexed surgeon (10)

blocks.note: Bones is slang for a doctor or surgeon, as in sawbones

annotation.surface: A picture of an irritated surgeon examining a skull.
annotation.walkthrough: The skull suggests an X-ray in a surgery; the definition is the pirate flag's skull and crossbones.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by association: the two thigh bones laid in an X under the skull on the Jolly Roger and on poison labels.

entries.clue: High and low part missing with spoiled print (10)

indicators.note: 'missing' means lacking, so LOW goes without the with letter
what is spoiled is ruined, its letters knocked out of order

blocks.note: W = with, the letter that goes missing

annotation.surface: A print ruined in places, with bits of it gone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High and low' sounds like a search everywhere; the words are fodder, and 'missing with' strips W from LOW before the shuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by genus: a print made from a flat stone or plate treated so ink sticks only to the image.

entries.clue: Engine hurling stones but three caught somehow (9)

indicators.note: 'somehow' means in some unspecified way, so the letters come in some other order

annotation.surface: A siege machine flings stones, yet somehow three are caught.
annotation.walkthrough: An engine here is the old sense, a machine of war.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the medieval counterweight catapult, an engine of war in the old sense of engine.

entries.clue: Book last character in time (4)

indicators.note: 'in' puts the last character within the word for time

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

annotation.surface: A novel's final character turns up just in time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Book' invites B or a novel; it is a book of the Bible, and 'last character' is Z rather than a figure in a story.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the historical books of the Old Testament.

entries.clue: Frequently visits topless consort — fair game? (4,5)

indicators.note: without its top, so the first letter comes off the visits word

blocks.note: HAUNTS without its first letter H
to consort with = to ally with

annotation.surface: A scandal sheet's question about someone who keeps visiting a topless companion.
annotation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a traditional British fairground or pub game of throwing sticks at a dummy's head; it also means anyone who is an easy target, hence 'fair game'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both at once: literally a game played at a fair, and idiomatically a person set up to be attacked.

entries.clue: Programme dropped Christmas broadcast (8)

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the words are taken by their sound

annotation.surface: A TV network pulls its Christmas show.
annotation.walkthrough: The homophone works with the British pronunciation SHED-yool, not the American SKED-jool.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as nouns: a planned timetable of events or broadcasts.

entries.clue: Journey starts in The Rip, ends in the outback (4)

indicators.note: 'starts' are beginnings, so the first letters of The Rip
'ends' are the final letters of the outback

annotation.surface: A trip that begins at a place called The Rip and finishes deep in the Australian bush.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starts' and 'ends' read as a travel itinerary; they pick letters. The capitals on The Rip make it look like a place name.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a twist of effort: a long arduous trip, originally an ox-wagon journey in South Africa.

entries.clue: Axe penetrates once he’s splintered shield (10)

indicators.note: to penetrate is to go into, so CUT goes inside the other letters
what is splintered breaks into pieces, so ONCE HES is rearranged

annotation.surface: A battle scene: an axe goes in and a shield shatters.
annotation.walkthrough: The axe and the shield belong to the same fight, which hides that 'axe' is the verb cut.
annotation.definitionFit: A heraldic term: the shield-shaped surface on which a coat of arms is displayed.

entries.clue: Salt gathering in massive quarry? (6)

blocks.note: surface reading: rock salt being dug out of a huge open pit
intended reading: a salt (old sailor) hauling in an enormous hunted animal

annotation.surface: Salt being collected from an enormous open-cast pit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Salt' is an old sailor, and the 'massive quarry' is the whale he hunts, not a pit; 'gathering in' is hauling in the catch.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a sailor (salt) whose quarry, the hunted animal, is the largest one in the sea.

entries.clue: City in which a friend curtailed addiction? (3,5)

indicators.note: curtailed literally means 'tail cut off', so the addiction word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a habit is an addiction; curtailed to HABI

annotation.surface: A city where a companion's dependency was cut short.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the fact that the wordplay does not really happen in the city: the city is just the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the capital of the United Arab Emirates.

entries.clue: Partners in crime with Abraham and Eliot? (5)

annotation.surface: Abraham Lincoln and T. S. Eliot cast as a criminal double act.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Partners in crime' is read as a verb: to abet someone is to partner them in a crime.
annotation.definitionFit: Read as a verb phrase: to help or encourage someone in wrongdoing is to partner them in crime.
annotation.definitionNote: 'Partners' is the verb, third person singular, matching the answer

entries.clue: Have no users partially connected to vital supply network (6)

indicators.note: 'partially' means in part, so only part of the phrase is used

annotation.surface: A utility complains it has no customers on its supply grid.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'vital supply network' is the body's system of veins, not a utility grid.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning description: the veins form the network carrying blood, a supply vital to life.

entries.clue: Single run stopped by wicket keeper (5)

indicators.note: a thing stopped by a plug has the plug in it, so the wicket letter sits inside the single-and-run letters

annotation.surface: A cricket scene: a quick single cut off by the wicketkeeper.
annotation.walkthrough: The cricket picture makes 'wicket keeper' one fielder; split it, and a keeper is someone who keeps.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the keeper of a shop, pub or pet is the person it belongs to.

entries.clue: Missile beginning to climb in south of France (4)

indicators.note: 'beginning' takes only the first letter of climb
'in' places that letter within the French word for south

annotation.surface: A rocket starts to rise over the south of France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South of France' reads as the Riviera; it means the French word for south.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Soviet-designed ballistic missile made famous in the 1991 Gulf War.

entries.clue: Letters inside shelter disturbed woman (5)

indicators.note: 'inside' keeps only the interior letters of shelter, dropping its ends
what is disturbed is thrown out of order, so those letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A woman sheltering indoors, upset by letters she has received.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like post; it is the word's own inner letters. A woman in crosswords is often just a woman's name.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword convention: 'woman' can stand for any female first name, and this is an old-fashioned English one.

entries.clue: No change in state active under cover of darkness (9)

indicators.note: 'in' places the change word within the state abbreviation

annotation.surface: A report that nothing has changed in the country's night-time operations.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No change' reads as one phrase; NO stands alone, and 'change in state' is TURN in CAL.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: from Latin nox, night, said of animals such as owls that wake after dark.

entries.clue: Content to defend a Murdoch mocked (9)

indicators.note: a defender surrounds and shields what it protects, so the content word wraps round the Murdoch

blocks.note: Iris Murdoch, the novelist, is one Murdoch

annotation.surface: A media story: a Murdoch defended, then ridiculed.
annotation.walkthrough: The name suggests the newspaper owner Rupert; the Murdoch meant is the novelist Iris, and 'Content' is the adjective, not material.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: ridiculed through wit or parody.

entries.clue: Almost losing lead in advance (5)

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so its first letter comes off

blocks.note: nearly = almost; minus its first letter N

annotation.surface: A race commentator: a runner almost gives up the lead while ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as first place in a race; here it is the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: before the expected time, ahead of schedule.
